quandoUsar: An action that cycles through a few related states in the same place, like Follow, Following, and Unfollow.
Short submissions with a transient confirmation: “Send invoice” becomes “Sending”, then “Sent”, and returns to the start on its own with `holdFor`.
When each state needs its own icon and tone (`neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, or `quiet`).
quandoEvitar: Use `action-button` when there is a single action with pending and done states and you do not want to describe states.
Use `split-button` when the person chooses among alternatives: here each click only advances to the next state in the list.
Use `switch` when the control represents an on or off setting, not an action.

teclado.acao: Advance to the next state in `states` (after the last, back to the first), calling `onAction` first.

acessibilidade: It is a `<button>` whose `aria-label` follows the visible label; while `onAction` runs, it gets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` and stays focusable.
Each change is announced by a `role="status"` next to the button: the new `label`, the `pendingLabel`, or the `failureLabel`.
Without a `pendingLabel` on the target state, the wait announcement is the fixed text “Working”; set `pendingLabel` and `failureLabel` (default “Try again”) in the interface language.
movimento: Letters shared at the start and end of the label stay still and the new ones rise from a slight blur, in sequence, while the width follows a spring with no overshoot.
Without `pendingLabel`, the pill folds into a circle with a spinner while the Promise runs (at least 450 ms); a failure shows `failureLabel` for 1.8 s and returns to the current state.
With “reduce motion”, letters and icons swap with a 0.12 s fade, the width jumps, and the spinner does not spin.
responsivo: Labels do not wrap and the pill changes width with each state; keep each `label` short.
desempenho: Each letter of the label is an animated element and there is one `ResizeObserver` per button: it suits short labels, not sentences.
notasIA: Describe the states in `states` (`id`, `label`, `icon`, `tone`) in cycle order; with fewer than two states the button is disabled.
`onAction(next, current)` runs before the swap: return a Promise to show the wait phase and reject it to display `failureLabel`.
Control the state with `value` and `onValueChange` or leave it internal with `defaultValue`; `holdFor` on a state makes the button advance on its own after that time.
